title: Preliminary Evaluation of Amber Glass Bottles for Naledbioassays Against Aedes Aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae)
content: The bottle bioassay is a method for detecting insecticide resistance in mosquito populations. Naled (dimethyl 1,2-dibromo-2,2-dichloroethylphosphate) is the active ingredient in many products used in mosquito control operations. Naled is photolabile, its half-life and rate of decay depend on temperature and humidity. Amber glass is used to protect the contents of the glassware container from photodegradation. This study was initiated to determine whether amber bottles rather than flint glass bottles could be used in bottle bioassays to protect the concentration of naled within the bottles from degradation due to light exposure, and to evaluate the effects of different light sources and the effects of leaving bottle caps on or off. Time to mortality data were collected. Effects of pesticide chemistry, pesticide formulation, bottle chemistry, light source, and sex of mosquitoes are discussed. Generally, mosquitoes died more quickly in the amber bottles, mosquitoes died more quickly in capped bottles than those left uncapped, and males died more quickly than females.
